label: Pocket money
blurb: Your family gives you money each month, sometimes late. No bank account yet; you use the family phone for UPI.

stageIntro.1: Intermediate, second year. Money comes from home, a little at a time, and it has to last.
stageIntro.2: Five years later… your first salary lands in your own account. Home still asks what you're saving.
stageIntro.3: Six more years… a raise, a family of your own, and bigger decisions.

label: Scholarship
blurb: Your ePASS allowance lands in your own bank account as one lump, plus a little from family. The phone at home is shared.

stageIntro.1: Intermediate, second year. The allowance just landed, all at once, and it has to last for months.
stageIntro.2: Five years later… a monthly salary. No more waiting for the allowance, and relatives with expectations.
stageIntro.3: Six more years… a raise, EMI offers everywhere, and younger cousins asking how you made it.

label: Earner
blurb: You work evenings at a shop. Pay is weekly and uneven, and part of it goes home. Own phone, own UPI.

stageIntro.1: Intermediate, second year. College by day, shifts by evening, and part of every pay goes home.
stageIntro.2: Five years later… a steady salary for the first time. Home still counts on you.
stageIntro.3: Six more years… you earn more, and so do the people trying to take it from you.
